answer: One effective defence is a stake-bonded reputation kernel: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and build a verifiable work history before it can transact at full limits. New identities start throttled, so a flood of fake accounts cannot outvote or drain a market in one tide of sign-ups; each fake must pay the same deposit and wait out the same probation. A periodic pulse check — random audits of recent work, counterpart signatures and stake still locked — revokes identities that fail, making a Sybil attack scale linearly in cost while honest agents keep their accumulated reputation.
